question: An open box is constructed by starting with a rectangular sheet of metal \(10\) in. by \(14\) in. and cutting a square of side \(x\) inches from each corner. The resulting projections are folded up and the seams welded. The volume of the resulting box is:
solution:
Each base dimension loses \(x\) inches at both ends, while the folded sides have height \(x\). Thus the box has base dimensions \(10-2x\) and \(14-2x\), in inches.

Volume is length times width times height, so
\[
V=x(10-2x)(14-2x)
=x(140-48x+4x^2).
\]
Therefore
\[
V=140x-48x^2+4x^3
\]
in cubic inches, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).

A nondegenerate box requires \(0<x<5\). At \(x=0\) the height vanishes, and at \(x=5\) the shorter base dimension vanishes.
